description_good_justification: The README and documentation site open with what the action does: suggest semantic version bumps and generate changelogs from commits with an LLM.
interact_justification: The README explains how to use the action (Quick start), report bugs (GitHub issues) and contribute (CONTRIBUTING.md): https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action#contributing
contribution_justification: Contribution process (fork, branch, pull request, CI, review): https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: Requirements (Ruff lint and format, zizmor, tests, Conventional Commits, SHA-pinned actions): https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements
sites_https_justification: Repository, documentation and releases are served by GitHub and GitHub Pages over HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: searchable, addressable by URL, no proprietary software needed. https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/issues
english_justification: All documentation is in English; issues are accepted in English.
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when.
repo_interim_justification: All work is merged through pull requests on master between releases.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag: https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/tags
version_tags_justification: Each release is a git tag (vX.Y.Z); release tags are protected and immutable.
release_notes_justification: Each GitHub release has human-readable release notes: https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known runtime vulnerabilities have been fixed in a release so far.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported in GitHub issues, as described in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs-and-requesting-features
report_responses_justification: No bug reports received yet; reports are acknowledged as they come in.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests received yet; they are answered as they come in.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, described in https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/blob/master/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports received in the last 6 months.
build_justification: Python scripts run directly from source; there is nothing to build. Dependencies are installed with uv from a hash-pinned lockfile.
test_justification: pytest suite in https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/blob/master/tests, run with `uv run pytest` and in CI.
test_invocation_justification: `uv run pytest`, the standard way for a Python project.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs tests, Ruff and zizmor on every pull request and push to master; tests are a required check: https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: New functionality and bug fixes must come with tests: https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent features came with tests, e.g. https://github.com/lmgarret/llm-release-action/pull/18 added tests/test_instructions_and_links.py.
warnings_justification: Ruff lint (pycodestyle, Pyflakes, isort, pyupgrade, bugbear) and zizmor for workflows, run in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any Ruff or zizmor finding.
warnings_strict_justification: Ruff runs with pycodestyle, Pyflakes, isort, pyupgrade and flake8-bugbear rules; zizmor runs at its default strictness.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies least privilege, input validation and defense in depth; see the security model: https://lmgarret.github.io/llm-release-action/explanation/security-model/
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the main risks for this kind of software (prompt injection, script injection in GitHub Actions, supply-chain attacks) and mitigates them; see SECURITY.md.
crypto_published_justification: The action does not implement or choose cryptography; network calls use HTTPS through standard libraries.
crypto_call_justification: The action does not use cryptography directly.
crypto_floss_justification: The action does not use cryptography directly.
crypto_keylength_justification: The action does not use cryptography directly.
crypto_working_justification: The action does not use cryptography directly.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The action does not use cryptography directly.
crypto_pfs_justification: The action does not use cryptography directly.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The action does not store passwords.
crypto_random_justification: The action does not generate cryptographic keys. Random prompt nonces and output delimiters use Python's secrets module.
delivery_mitm_justification: Delivered through GitHub over HTTPS; users are told to pin the action to a full commit SHA. Python dependencies are installed with --require-hashes.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are retrieved over HTTP; dependency hashes are committed in the lockfile.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity in the software produced. Dependabot security updates are enabled.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Dependabot security updates are enabled and merged promptly.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled; no alerts.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Python and GitHub Actions), Ruff and zizmor run on every pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL security queries and zizmor (GitHub Actions security) look for common vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No open CodeQL or zizmor findings; zizmor is a required check.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every pull request and push to master.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or other dynamic analysis tool beyond the test suite.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests run with Python assertions enabled.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is used.
